newsitem.title: USA: Healthdyne stock jumps as Georgia rejects measure.
newsitem.headline: Healthdyne stock jumps as Georgia rejects measure.

text.p: The stock of medical device firm Healthdyne Technologies Inc. rose sharply Wednesday on views Invacare Corp. will aggressively pursue a $166 million hostile takeover following the rejection of a Georgia legislative measure that could have crushed its effort.

The stock of Marietta, Ga.-based Healthdyne gained $1.625 to $13.25 on Nasdaq in afternoon trading -- about where it had been trading before the legislative action earlier this month sent the shares tumbling to about $11.
"The (takeover) fight is not over, but it has been made less difficult," said one trader of takeover stocks.
Healthdyne repeatedly has rejected medical equipment company Invacare's $13-per-share offer, saying that the company is not for sale.

Elyria, Ohio-based Invacare's hostile effort was dealt a near-fatal blow last week when the Georgia Senate approved a measure to require public companies to stagger the election of board directors. The measure would have severely curtailed any hostile takeover attempts in which an unwelcome bidder sought to take control by replacing a company's board.

The measure itself was dealt a setback on Tuesday when the state's House of Representatives voted against it and sent it back to the Senate. The measure was expected to reach a House-Senate conference committee on Thursday.

Wall Street sources expect Invacare, which had blasted the Georgia legislative effort, to now pursue its takeover by trying to replace Healthdyne's board at the company's yet-unscheduled annual shareholders meeting. Invacare last week announced that it planned to nominate a slate of seven directors.
Invacare first offered to buy Healthdyne in January for $12.50 per share. After its offer was rejected, Invacare raised its bid to $13 and launched a tender offer for Healthdyne stock.
The latest Gerogia action "certainly gives Invacare an incentive to hang in there," said Steven Cohen, head of research at New York arbitrage firm Kellner, DiLeo & Co.
Wall Street sources said Healthdyne shares may edge up to more than $14 in the near-term as Invacare moves ahead with its effort. Shares of Invacare, also on Nasdaq, gained $1.25 to $24.50.
